entities.summary: Chamlong Srimuang is a Thai activist and former politician. A former general, he was a leader of the "Young Turks" military clique, founded and led the Palang Dharma Party, served for six years as governor of Bangkok, led the anti-military uprising of May 1992, and is a prominent member of the People's Alliance for Democracy, a group strongly opposed to former prime minister Thaksin Shinawatra. Chamlong had supported the military junta that overthrew Thaksin in a coup. A devout Buddhist and follower of the Santi Asoke sect, he is now celibate, a vegetarian, and claims to have no worldly possessions.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a leader of the anti-military uprising of May 1992 and a prominent member of the People's Alliance for Democracy, Chamlong Srimuang played a significant role in shaping Thailand's political landscape following Thaksin Shinawatra's ouster. His actions contributed to the country's transition towards democracy.
